title: Juniper and the Letters
premise: Petra Almeida inherited her grandmother's vineyard along with a mountain of debt, and she's spent three years keeping the estate alive through sheer stubbornness and silence. When a clerical error surfaces an old orchard deed bearing both her name and that of Juniper Reyes—the botanist who once loved her and left to save a career—Petra must confront the woman she buried with the past. As the harvest festival approaches, Juniper returns to contest or claim the land, and old tenderness resurfaces against Petra's fear that love is another debt she can't afford. In the end, Petra chooses visibility over survival-by-invisibility: she sells half the vineyard to save the whole, signs the deed alongside Juniper, and they plant the orchard together as the festival lights come on.
about_author: Lena Underhill is the pen name of a former agricultural journalist who spent a decade covering family farms before turning to fiction about the people who refuse to let them die. She writes from a converted barn in wine country, where she keeps a wall of unsent letters as research.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. While preparing loan paperwork, Petra discovers the orchard parcel's deed lists two names: hers and Juniper Reyes, the woman who left her eleven years ago. The bank threatens foreclosure unless ownership is clarified before the festival. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by grief, as Petra realizes the past has legal standing after all.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper arrives to contest the deed but finds a crate of unsent letters Petra wrote during their separation, hidden among her grandmother's things. Reading them, she understands why Petra pushed her away—to protect her career. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into longing, and the first crack in Juniper's resolve to leave again.

chapters.title: Festival of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On festival eve, the bank's final notice arrives just as Juniper offers to buy the orchard outright—an act Petra reads as pity, not love. A public argument at the lantern lighting exposes both women's fears: duty versus devotion. Emotional beat: climax; love declared in anger, then nearly destroyed by pride.

chapters.title: What We Plant Together
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Dawn after the festival: Petra rejects the all-or-nothing sale, instead selling half the vineyard to clear the debt and co-signing the deed with Juniper freely. They read the last letter aloud over turned soil and plant the first tree. Emotional beat: resolution; choosing each other not despite the cost, but with eyes open to it.
